name: Eperisone + Aceclofenac
meta: Schedule H – prescription only; Aceclofenac: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: Phenylacetic acid derivative (glycolic ester of diclofenac)
White crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water (BCS Class II).

Eperisone Hydrochloride: Developed in Japan and widely used in Asia for spastic paralysis and musculoskeletal spasm; marketed in India in IR and SR forms. First approval/introduction: Japan 1983 (Eisai).

Aceclofenac: A glycolic acid ester of diclofenac developed in Spain; widely used in Europe and India for osteoarthritis, RA and ankylosing spondylitis. First approval/introduction: Patented 1983; approved 1992 (Prodesfarma / Almirall, Spain).
Once-daily SR combination: eperisone relaxes muscle with vasodilatory action without sedation; aceclofenac provides anti-inflammatory analgesia.

Eperisone Hydrochloride Inhibits spinal mono- and polysynaptic reflexes and gamma-motor neuron activity, reduces muscle spindle sensitivity, and has vasodilator action that improves muscle blood flow – relieving spasticity and myotonia with little sedation. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits spinal reflexes and gamma-motor neurone activity; vasodilator action improves muscle blood flow; suppresses pain reflex.

Aceclofenac Inhibits cyclo-oxygenase (preferential COX-2) reducing prostaglandin synthesis; also inhibits IL-1 and TNF and stimulates cartilage matrix synthesis. Analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits COX (preferential COX-2) and suppresses IL-1beta and TNF; stimulates glycosaminoglycan synthesis in cartilage.
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 1.6–1.9 h; extensive first-pass metabolism. Half-life ~1.6–1.8 h (sustained-release prolongs action for once-daily dosing).
Hepatic – CYP2C9 to 4'-hydroxyaceclofenac (main), small amounts of diclofenac
Summary: Rapid, complete absorption; Tmax 1.25–3 h. >99% protein bound. Metabolised to 4'-hydroxyaceclofenac and diclofenac (CYP2C9). Half-life ~4 h.
Acute low back pain with muscle spasm
Cervical spondylosis, periarthritis of shoulder with spasm
Painful musculoskeletal disorders requiring anti-inflammatory and muscle-relaxant therapy
One tablet once daily after meals
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use only if benefit outweighs risk.
Avoid in severe impairment (CrCl <30); monitor creatinine in mild–moderate impairment.
Mild: reduce to 100 mg/day; severe: contraindicated.
Higher risk of GI bleeding, renal impairment and CV events – lowest dose, shortest time; consider gastroprotection (PPI).
Hypersensitivity, or asthma/urticaria/rhinitis triggered by aspirin or other NSAIDs
Active peptic ulcer or GI bleeding; history of recurrent ulceration
Cardiovascular thrombotic events (MI, stroke) – use lowest dose for shortest time
GI ulceration, bleeding and perforation – higher risk in elderly, with steroids, anticoagulants, SSRIs
Hepatotoxicity – monitor LFTs on long-term use
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics (reduced effect, renal impairment)
Aceclofenac: Take after food or with milk; avoid alcohol (GI bleeding).
Eperisone Hydrochloride: LFTs and renal function on long-term use.
Aceclofenac: BP, renal function, LFTs and CBC on prolonged use; signs of GI bleeding.
Eperisone Hydrochloride: Supportive care. Aceclofenac: Nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, GI bleeding, renal failure, convulsions (rare). Supportive care; activated charcoal.
May cause drowsiness or weakness – caution while driving
Do not combine with other painkillers containing NSAIDs
Report black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, swelling
Use for the shortest time needed
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
